proposals.before: In ancient times Zheng Wu Gong wished to attack Hu, thus he married his son to them.
proposals.after: In ancient times Zheng Wu Gong wished to attack Hu, thus he married his daughter to their ruler.
proposals.reason: 「以其子妻之」means he gave his daughter in marriage (妻 as verb); translating 子 as "son" reverses the marriage relation.

proposals.after: In ancient times Zheng Wu Gong wished to attack Hu, thus married his daughter to them.
proposals.reason: 「以其子妻之」is marrying off a daughter; "son" misreads the kinship and verb 妻.

proposals.before: Therefore, these two sons, all sages, yet could not avoid debasing their persons and entering the world in such filth, then this is not what able service establishes.
proposals.after: Therefore, these two men, both sages, yet could not avoid debasing their persons and entering the world in such filth; then this is not what those able to serve establish.
proposals.reason: 二子者 means these two men/masters, not literal "sons"; also 非能仕之所設也 is misread.

decisions.reason: 伊尹 is the personal name Yi Yin; the fused lowercase "yiyin" is a real error, and the proposed capitalization/spacing is accurate without other change.
The literal field likewise fails to render 伊尹 as the name Yi Yin; correcting "yiyin" to "Yi Yin" matches the Chinese without semantic invention.

以其子妻之 uses 妻 as a verb 'to give as wife,' so 子 here is a daughter given in marriage to Hu's side; "married his son" reverses the marital relation, and the proposed daughter-to-ruler wording restores it.
The literal likewise misreads 妻之 as marrying a son; replacing "son" with "daughter" correctly reflects giving the child as a wife to Hu.
二子者 refers to Yi Yin and Baili Xi as two gentlemen, not sons; 皆 with two people is "both," and 非能仕之所設也 is better rendered as what those able to serve establish than "able service establishes."
